title: Verifying a Synchronous FIFO: Corners That Bite
description: How I verify a synchronous FIFO with a queue-based scoreboard, flag assertions and targeted coverage.
content:
Synchronous FIFOs look simple: a memory, a write pointer and a read pointer. Most FIFO bugs hide at the boundaries, though: the cycle it fills, the cycle it drains, and the cycle a read and a write happen together.

This post walks through how I approach verifying one.

## What the design promises

A FIFO's contract is short:

- Data comes out in the same order it went in.
- `full` asserts when no more writes can be accepted, and `empty` when nothing is left to read.
- A write while full, or a read while empty, changes nothing.

Every check below traces back to one of these lines.

## The handshake

Here is a write of two words followed by a read, with `full` and `empty` tracking occupancy:

```wave
# Write two words, then read one back
clk   : p.........
wr_en : 0.1.0.....
wdata : x.=.x..... | A5 3C
rd_en : 0.....1.0.
empty : 1..0......
```

## A reference model in the scoreboard

The simplest scoreboard is a SystemVerilog queue that mirrors what the FIFO should hold:

```systemverilog
class fifo_scoreboard extends uvm_scoreboard;
  `uvm_component_utils(fifo_scoreboard)

  bit [7:0] model[$];

  function void write_wr(fifo_item t);
    if (!t.full) model.push_back(t.data);
  endfunction

  function void write_rd(fifo_item t);
    bit [7:0] exp;
    if (t.empty) return;
    exp = model.pop_front();
    if (t.data !== exp)
      `uvm_error("SB", $sformatf("Expected %0h, got %0h", exp, t.data))
  endfunction
endclass
```

> [!TIP]
> Sample `full` and `empty` on the same clock edge as the request. Sampling a cycle late is the most common source of false mismatches.

## Assertions for the flags

Assertions catch flag bugs at the exact cycle they happen:

```sva
// No write may land while the FIFO is full
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  full && wr_en |=> $stable(wr_ptr));

// empty and full are never both high
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  !(full && empty));
```

## Coverage that matters

| Scenario | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Write while full | Overflow protection |
| Read while empty | Underflow protection |
| Simultaneous read and write at full | Occupancy must stay constant |
| Pointer wrap-around | Off-by-one in address logic |

If all four bins are hit and the scoreboard stays clean, I trust the FIFO.

## Wrapping up

Model the contract, assert the flags, and cover the corners. That pattern carries over to almost every block I verify.
